Bug_Title: SING: Class using singleton design pattern has non-private constructor. (SING_SINGLETON_HAS_NONPRIVATE_CONSTRUCTOR)
Bug_Details:
This class is using singleton design pattern and has non-private constructor (please note that a default constructor might exist which is not private). Given that, it is possible to create a copy of the object, thus violating the singleton pattern.
The easier solution would be making the constructor private.
SEI CERT MSC07-J rule
Bug_Explanation: The SingletonExample class has a public constructor, allowing external code to create new instances of the class. This violates the singleton pattern, which is supposed to restrict instance creation to a single object. The constructor should be private to enforce the singleton constraint.
Trigger_Explanation: The testShowBug method calls the showBug method of SingletonExample, which creates another instance of the class using the public constructor, violating the singleton pattern. This results in a failed assertion that expects the same instance to be referenced twice.
